summary: The exact candidate is a verified partial fix for the production detokenizer's response-length-dependent U+FFFD stall under fixed-size decode events. It is not a full original-issue fix: the simulated-acceptance path still hardcodes token id 100, and the defensive bound counts events rather than limiting the retained token window itself.

tests.what_was_measured: Original failure on recorded base: repeated U+FFFD-producing byte tokens never committed text; 1 failed and 2 boundary cases passed. Raw output: /job/review-evidence/j-1736a88be7d8/base-regression.log
Candidate regression and neighboring stop-trimming coverage passed: 11 tests. Raw output: /job/review-evidence/j-1736a88be7d8/candidate-tests.log
The actual fixed-token GPU path still produced predict_unique=[100] on gfx950, proving Defect A remains. Raw output: /job/review-evidence/j-1736a88be7d8/candidate-gpu.log

One- and four-token events and empty decodes had response-length-independent live windows; 4096-token events retained roughly 53k-57k tokens, showing the bound is event-based rather than a token-tail cap. Raw output: /job/review-evidence/j-1736a88be7d8/candidate-adversarial.log

gpu_execution.evidence: One assigned AMD Instinct MI355X, gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-, executed the real candidate generate_simulated_accept_index path with Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 and synchronized before results were read.

remaining_counterexamples: Defect A is unchanged: fixed-token simulated acceptance still executes predict.fill_(100), so tokenizers where id 100 decodes to U+FFFD still manufacture the triggering stream.

The candidate limits consecutive stalled decode events, not retained tokens. An event containing 4096 invalid byte tokens left a live decode window above 53,000 tokens; therefore it is not a strict small-tail bound regardless of chunk size.
The exact DeepSeek-V4-Pro tokenizer, full serving semantics, and the reported eight-GPU workload remain unverified because weights and topology were unavailable.
remaining_limitations: DeepSeek-V4-Pro weights and the reported eight-GPU TP/DP/EAGLE deployment were unavailable, so throughput, TTFT, response semantics, and distributed serving behavior were not reproduced.
The deterministic byte-fallback tokenizer validates the real DetokenizerManager control flow but not the DeepSeek-V4-Pro vocabulary or model architecture.
The single gfx950 GPU fixture validates simulated-acceptance tensor execution only; it is not a model-serving reproduction.
No native source changed, repository-environment.json declared native=null, and therefore there was no native library to rebuild.
